## Evidence hierarchy

1. Official grader or exact official Mini-100 paired result
2. Rigorous proof or analytic identity
3. Frozen full-width holdout
4. Architecture-matched synthetic screen
5. Oracle diagnostic
6. Development-only result

Never promote a lower tier over a conflicting higher tier.

## Current frozen candidate

- Complete 66,048-point Kerdock rule
- Persistent blocked/assembly-free multiplication
- Three-layer suffix compiler
- Pilot: 8 columns per Kerdock basis, 2,064 total rows
- Rare threshold: 8
- First compiled-layer correction: irrelevant/zero
- Middle correction: 0
- Final correction: 0.875
- Full-suffix fallback when predicted cost ratio > 0.995

## Do not duplicate

- Static cubature/rotation/reweighting searches
- Kerdock-Stein transfer
- Quadratic first-layer controls
- Generic particle thinning or suffix-kernel Nyström
- Risk-penalized depth selectors
- c=7 pilot screens
- Runtime boundary audits
- Direct weights-to-Kerdock-residual prediction

## Required next experiment

Run a paired official Mini-100 comparison of:

1. Assembly-free Kerdock baseline
2. Frozen two-layer compiler
3. Fixed three-layer candidate
4. Adaptive 2–6-layer candidate

Record raw MSE, adjusted score, tracked/effective FLOPs, subprocess wall time, peak memory, per-network wins, worst degradation, compiler fallback count, padding/packing overhead, and bootstrap intervals.

No candidate replaces the protected estimator unless it wins after all accounting and has no material tail failures.
